Python

Complete Reference & Concept Guide v3.14 Cross-platform Released Oct 2026

Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its readability and versatility. This guide covers core syntax, data structures, OOP, and modern Python features up to 3.14.

Installation & Setup

# Download Python 3.14 from python.org or use a package manager

# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install python@3.14

# Ubuntu / Debian
sudo apt install python3.14 python3.14-venv python3.14-pip

# Windows (Chocolatey)
choco install python --version=3.14.0

# Verify installation
python --version
python -m pip --version

# Start the interactive REPL
python

Python CLI & pip Reference

Essential commands for Python development.

CommandDescription

Data Types

Python is dynamically typed. All values are objects with a type.

Primitive Types
# Numeric types
x = 42              # int (unbounded)
y = 3.14            # float (IEEE 754 double)
z = 1 + 2j           # complex
big = 1_000_000      # underscores as separators
hex_val = 0xff       # hexadecimal
bin_val = 0b1010     # binary

# Boolean
is_active = True      # bool (subclass of int)
is_done = False

# String (immutable sequence of Unicode codepoints)
name = "Hello"       # double quotes
char = 'A'           # single quotes
multi = """Multi-line
string"""
raw = r"c:\users\name"  # raw string (no escape)
fstr = f"Value {x}"    # f-string (Python 3.6+)

# NoneType
result = None         # null / absence of value
Type Conversion & Checking
# Explicit conversion
int("42")         # 42
float("3.14")      # 3.14
str(100)          # "100"
bool(1)           # True
list("abc")       # ['a', 'b', 'c']

# Type checking
isinstance(x, int)   # True
type(x)             # <class 'int'>

Collections (Data Structures)

Lists, Tuples, Sets, Dicts
# List â€” mutable ordered sequence
nums = [1, 2, 3]
nums.append(4)         # [1, 2, 3, 4]
nums.insert(0, 0)    # [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
nums.pop()              # removes & returns last
nums.sort()            # in-place sort
sliced = nums[1:3]   # [1, 2]

# Tuple â€” immutable ordered sequence
point = (10, 20)
x, y = point           # tuple unpacking

# Set â€” unordered, unique elements
unique = {1, 2, 3, 2}  # {1, 2, 3}
unique.add(4)
a & b                  # intersection
a | b                  # union
a - b                  # difference

# Dict â€” key-value mapping
user = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}
user["email"] = "a@b.com"
user.get("phone", "N/A")   # safe access with default
for k, v in user.items():
    print(k, v)
List Comprehensions
# Classic comprehension
squares = [x**2 for x in range(10)]
# [0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81]

# With condition
evens = [x for x in range(20) if x % 2 == 0]

# Dict comprehension
square_map = {x: x**2 for x in range(5)}

# Set comprehension
unique_lens = {len(w) for w in words}

# Generator expression (lazy)
total = sum(x**2 for x in range(100))

Control Flow

Conditionals & Loops
# if / elif / else
x = 10
if x > 0:
    print("positive")
elif x == 0:
    print("zero")
else:
    print("negative")

# Ternary expression
status = "adult" if age >= 18 else "minor"

# for loop (iterate over iterable)
for i in range(5):
    print(i)

for idx, val in enumerate(items):
    print(idx, val)

# while loop
while count > 0:
    count -= 1

# break / continue / else on loops
for n in nums:
    if n == target:
        break
else:
    print("not found")  # runs if no break

# match / case (Python 3.10+, structural pattern matching)
match command:
    case "start":
        start()
    case "stop":
        stop()
    case _:
        print("unknown")

Functions

Defining Functions
def greet(name: str, greeting: str = "Hello") -> str:
    """Return a greeting string."""
    return f"{greeting}, {name}!"

# *args (variable positional), **kwargs (variable keyword)
def log(*args, **kwargs):
    for a in args: print(a)
    for k, v in kwargs.items():
        print(f"{k} = {v}")

# Positional-only (/) and keyword-only (*) parameters
def div(a: float, b: float, /) -> float:
    return a / b

def config(*, debug: bool = False, timeout: int = 30):
    pass

# Lambda (anonymous function)
square = lambda x: x**2
nums.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
Decorators & Closures
# Decorator â€” a function that wraps another
def timer(func):
    import time
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        result = func(*args, **kwargs)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        print(f"{func.__name__} took {elapsed:.3f}s")
        return result
    return wrapper

@timer
def slow_func():
    return sum(range(10_000_000))

# functools.wraps preserves metadata
from functools import wraps

def log_calls(func):
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        print(f"Calling {func.__name__}")
        return func(*args, **kwargs)
    return wrapper

Classes & OOP

Class Definition
class User:
    """Base class for all users."""

    # Class variable (shared across all instances)
    role = "user"

    def __init__(self, name: str, email: str):
        # Instance variables
        self.name = name
        self.email = email

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.name}"

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "User":
        return cls(data["name"], data["email"])

    @staticmethod
    def validate_email(email: str) -> bool:
        return "@" in email

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"User({self.name!r}, {self.email!r})"
Inheritance & Magic Methods
class Admin(User):
    role = "admin"

    def __init__(self, name, email, permissions: list = None):
        super().__init__(name, email)
        self.permissions = permissions or []

# Magic (dunder) methods
class Vector:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x, self.y = x, y

    def __add__(self, other):   # +
        return Vector(self.x + other.x, self.y + other.y)

    def __eq__(self, other):     # ==
        return self.x == other.x and self.y == other.y

    def __str__(self):           # str()
        return f"Vector({self.x}, {self.y})"

Modules & Packages

# Import a module
import math
math.sqrt(16)

# Import specific names
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Alias
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# A package is a directory with __init__.py (can be empty)
# mypkg/
#   __init__.py
#   utils.py
#   models.py

# Conditional import with TYPE_CHECKING (avoids circular)
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .models import Product

Error Handling

# try / except / else / finally
try:
    result = risky / divisor
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("Cannot divide by zero")
except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
    print(f"Invalid operation: {e}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Unexpected: {e}")
else:
    print(f"Result: {result}")  # runs if no exception
finally:
    cleanup()                     # always runs

# Raise exceptions
raise ValueError("Invalid input")
raise RuntimeError("Something went wrong") from cause

# Custom exception
class AppError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, code=500):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code

File I/O

# Context manager (auto-closes file)
with open("data.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    content = f.read()          # entire file as string
    lines = f.readlines()        # list of lines
    for line in f:              # iterate lazily
        print(line.strip())

# Writing
with open("out.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("Hello\n")
    f.writelines(["line1\n", "line2\n"])

# Modes: r (read), w (write), a (append), r+ (read+write)
# Binary: rb, wb

# Pathlib (modern file paths)
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("config/settings.json")
data = p.read_text()           # read as string
p.write_text(json_str)        # write string
json.loads(p.read_text())

Virtual Environments

Isolate project dependencies to avoid version conflicts.

venv (built-in)
# Create environment
python -m venv .venv

# Activate
# macOS / Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install packages (isolated)
pip install requests pytest

# Freeze dependencies
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# Deactivate
deactivate
uv â€” Fast Package Manager (Modern Alternative)
# Install uv (Rust-based, 10-100x faster than pip)
pip install uv

# Create venv & sync
uv venv
uv pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run scripts with automatic venv
uv run python script.py

Type Hints (PEP 484)

Optional static typing. Checked by mypy, pyright, or pylance.

from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Union, Any, Callable
from typing import TypeVar, Generic

T = TypeVar("T")

def first(items: List[T]) -> Optional[T]:
    return items[0] if items else None

# Union (one of multiple types)
def parse_id(id: str | int) -> int:  # Python 3.10+ syntax
    return int(id)

# Callable[[ArgType], ReturnType]
def run_hook(hook: Callable[[str], None], data: str):
    hook(data)

# TypedDict â€” typed dictionary
from typing import TypedDict
class Movie(TypedDict):
    title: str
    year: int
    rating: float

# Dataclass (auto-generates __init__, __repr__, etc.)
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Point:
    x: float
    y: float
    z: float = 0.0

Async / Await

Concurrent code using async/await syntax (PEP 492, Python 3.5+).

import asyncio

async def fetch_data(url: str) -> dict:
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as resp:
            return await resp.json()

async def main():
    # Run multiple tasks concurrently
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        fetch_data("https://api1.example.com"),
        fetch_data("https://api2.example.com"),
    )
    print(results)

# Entry point
asyncio.run(main())

# Async context managers & iterators
class AsyncCounter:
    async def __aiter__(self):
        return self
    async def __anext__(self):
        if self.n >= 5: raise StopAsyncIteration
        self.n += 1
        return self.n

Testing

unittest (built-in)
import unittest

class TestMath(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_add(self):
        self.assertEqual(add(2, 3), 5)

    def test_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            validate("")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
pytest (third-party, most popular)
# test_math.py
import pytest

def test_add():
    assert add(2, 3) == 5

def test_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate("")

@pytest.mark.parametrize("a,b,expected", [
    (1, 2, 3),
    (0, 0, 0),
])
def test_params(a, b, expected):
    assert add(a, b) == expected
▶ Run tests: python -m unittest discover — or — pytest -v --cov=src (with coverage)

Best Practices

Code Style
  • Follow PEP 8 â€” 4-space indentation, 88 chars line length
  • Use black for automatic formatting
  • Use ruff for linting (fast, Rust-based)
  • Snake case for functions/variables: my_function
  • Pascal case for classes: MyClass
  • Constants in UPPER_CASE: MAX_RETRIES
Project Structure
  • Use src/ layout or flat module per project
  • Always use virtual environments
  • Pin dependencies in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml
  • Write type hints for all public APIs
  • Use pathlib over os.path
  • Prefer f-strings over .format() or %
Performance
  • Use __slots__ for memory-efficient classes
  • Prefer list.append over list += [item]
  • Use generator expressions over lists for large data
  • Profile with cProfile or py-spy
  • Consider numpy for numerical heavy-lifting
Security
  • Never use eval() or exec() on untrusted input
  • Use secrets module, not random, for crypto
  • Sanitize with shlex.quote() for shell commands
  • Regularly update dependencies (pip-audit)
  • Use hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac for password hashing
▶ Recommended Tools: ruff (linter) · black (formatter) · mypy (type checker) · pytest (testing) · uv (package mgmt) · pre-commit (hooks)
